STATE OF VERMONT 
PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION 
 
Case No. 19-2932-PET  
 
Petition of Vermont Gas Systems, Inc. for 
approval of an Alternative Regulation Plan, 
pursuant to 30 V.S.A. § 218d 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Order entered: 
 
 
ORDER APPROVING EXTENSION OF ALTERNATIVE REGULATION PLAN 
 
In this Order, the Vermont Public Utility Commission adopts the following proposal for 
decision and approves the petition filed by Vermont Gas Systems, Inc. (“Vermont Gas” or 
“VGS”) for a one-year extension of its existing alternative regulation plan (the “Current Plan”) 
approved in Case No. 18-2033-PET and previously approved by the Commission in Case No. 
17-3861-PET and Docket 8698. 
 
PROPOSAL FOR DECISION 
I. 
PROCEDURAL HISTORY  
On July 3, 2019, Vermont Gas filed a petition with the Commission requesting approval 
of a one-year extension (the “Successor Plan”) of the Current Plan to enable continued 
implementation of existing provisions, including the purchase gas adjustment.  Vermont Gas 
states that it intends to file an updated proposed alternative regulation plan for a longer term that 
includes provisions addressing other components of its cost of service, including the non-gas 
costs, by August 31, 2019 (the “Next Plan”).1   
On July 22, 2019, I issued a procedural order seeking comments on the proposed 
Successor Plan by August 2, 2019.  A copy of the order was provided to all parties in Case Nos. 
18-2033-PET and 17-3861-PET and Docket 8698. 
On August 2, 2019, the Vermont Department of Public Service (“Department”) filed 
comments on the Successor Plan.  The Department states that “ratepayer interests will be best

served” by approving the Successor Plan.2  The Department explains that its support “is 
contingent on VGS’s commitment to file a proposed alternative regulation plan [the Next Plan] 
that more thoroughly addresses the broader policy objectives set by the Commission in its July 
23, 2018, Order in Case No. 17-3142-PET.”3 
No other comments on the Successor Plan were filed.      
On August 9, 2019, Vermont Gas filed a response to the Department’s comments.  
Vermont Gas informs the Commission that due to the internal review schedule, Vermont Gas 
anticipates that its Next Plan will be filed later than previously stated.  Vermont Gas nowstates 
that it “is committed” to filing the Next Plan by no later than September 13, 2019. 
No party requests a hearing or objects to the prefiled testimony and exhibits filed by 
Vermont Gas.  Accordingly, the Petition, the prefiled testimony of Eileen Simollardes, and 
exhibits EMS-1 and EMS-2 are admitted into evidence as if presented at a hearing.  
Pursuant to 30 V.S.A. § 8(c), and based on the record and evidence before me, I present 
the following proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law to the Commission. 
II.  FINDINGS 
1. Vermont Gas is currently regulated under an alternative regulation plan approved by 
the Commission in Docket 8698 on January 20, 2017, on August 31, 2017, in Case No. 17-3861-
PET, and again on August 14, 2018, in Case No. 18-2003-PET (the “Current Plan”). Simollardes 
pf. at 2. 
2. The Current Plan is scheduled to expire on September 30, 2019.  Simollardes pf. at 2. 
3. Vermont Gas proposes to implement a Successor Plan that is substantially identical to 
the Current Plan but that amends the effective date to be October 1, 2019, and the expiration date 
to be September 30, 2020.  Simollardes pf. at 5; exh. EMS-1. 
4. The Current Plan is comprised of four discrete regulatory provisions, including the 
purchase gas adjustment, weather normalization provisions, service quality and reliability 
requirements, and report and dispute resolution provisions.  These provisions will remain 
unchanged in the Successor Plan.  Simollardes pf. at 4; exh. EMS-1. 
 
2 Department comments at 1.

Case No. 19-2932-PET

5. The provisions of the Current Plan do not regulate or affect VGS’s non-gas rates, 
which are governed under traditional rate regulation and are currently under review by the 
Commission in Case No. 19-0513-TF.  Simollardes pf. at 4. 
 
III. 
DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION 
Vermont Gas requests approval of a Successor Plan that is a one-year extension of the 
Current Plan.  The Commission previously found that the Current Plan is in the public interest 
and meets the statutory criteria of 30 V.S.A. § 218d.4  Given that the only change in the 
Successor Plan requested by Vermont Gas is to amend the effective date and expiration date of 
the Current Plan, and that no parties to Docket 8698 or Case Nos. 17-3861-PET or 18-2033-PET 
object to the requested extension, the Commission concludes that the Successor Plan also meets 
those standards.  Accordingly, the request to adopt the Successor Plan is approved. 
We note that the Department stated that its support of the Successor Plan is based on 
Vermont Gas’s representation that it would file the Next Plan by August 31, 2019.  Vermont Gas 
subsequently notified the Commission and the Department that it is committed to filing the Next 
Plan by no later than September 13, 2019.  As a condition of our approval of the Successor Plan 
and as committed to in its filings in this proceeding, Vermont Gas shall file a more expansive 
alternative regulation plan by no later than September 13, 2019.

IV. 
ORDER 
IT IS HEREBY ORDERED, ADJUDGED, AND DECREED by the Vermont Public Utility 
Commission (“Commission”) that: 
1. The findings, conclusions, and recommendations of the Hearing Officer are adopted. 
2. The amended alternative regulation plan filed by Vermont Gas Systems, Inc. 
(“Vermont Gas”) on July 3, 2019, in this proceeding and marked as exhibit EMS-1, the 
“Successor Plan,” is approved.  
3. On October 1, 2019, the alternative regulation plan approved by the Commission in 
its August 14, 2018, Order in Case No. 18-2033-PET shall cease to have effect and shall be 
replaced by the Successor Plan. 
4.   As committed to in its filings in this proceeding,Vermont Gas shall file a more 
expansive proposed alternative regulation plan with the Commission by no later than September 
13, 2019.
